Since \(x^2+y^2=1\), we have \(-1\le x,y\le 1\). Thus
\[
\sqrt{x^2-4x+4}=|x-2|=2-x.
\]
Also,
\[
xy-3x+y-3=(x+1)(y-3).
\]
Here \(x+1\ge 0\) and \(y-3<0\), so \((x+1)(y-3)\le 0\). For the square root to be real, we need
\[
(x+1)(y-3)=0.
\]
Since \(y-3\neq 0\), we get \(x=-1\). Then \(x^2+y^2=1\) gives
\[
1+y^2=1 \implies y=0.
\]
So the expression equals
\[
|x-2|+\sqrt{(x+1)(y-3)}
=|-1-2|+0=3.
\]
\[
\boxed{3}
\]
